front_blocks.md: What is the role of the base class in an inheritance hierarchy?

back_blocks.md: The base class is the **blueprint or template from which the derived class inherits**, defining the common properties and behaviours shared among multiple derived classes.

front_blocks.md: Why does the constructor of a derived class call the constructor of its base class?

back_blocks.md: So that the **attributes belonging to the base class are initialised**, before the derived class sets its own additional attributes.

front_blocks.md: Define **encapsulation**.

back_blocks.md: Encapsulation is the practice of **grouping data (attributes) and methods (functions) together within a class**.

cards.front_md: Define **encapsulation**.
cards.back_md: Encapsulation is the practice of **grouping data (attributes) and methods (functions) together within a class**.

front_blocks.md: How does encapsulation keep data secure?

back_blocks.md: It **controls access to the data using access modifiers** such as public and private, so the data cannot be accidentally modified or misused.

cards.front_md: How does encapsulation keep data secure?
cards.back_md: It **controls access to the data using access modifiers** such as public and private, so the data cannot be accidentally modified or misused.

front_blocks.md: State two benefits of encapsulation other than security.

back_blocks.md: It **organises code by keeping related data and methods together**, and it **promotes code reusability**, so the same class can be used in different parts of a program without rewriting it.

cards.front_md: State two benefits of encapsulation other than security.
cards.back_md: It **organises code by keeping related data and methods together**, and it **promotes code reusability**, so the same class can be used in different parts of a program without rewriting it.
